title: Printed shapes on a centimetre grid
subject: Mathematics
unit: Spring 2: Decimals and percentages; perimeter and area; statistics
source: Seeded from mathematics/y5 lessons 48, 49, 50, 51, 52 (Printed shapes on a centimetre grid)
intro: To understand how to calculate the perimeter of rectangles

blocks.text: Copy each shape from the slides onto the grid, then find its perimeter and area by counting.

questions.q: 7 cm by 4 cm. Perimeter?
A square with sides 6 m. Perimeter?
Perimeter 40 cm, length 12 cm. Width?
L-shape: outer sides 9 cm and 5 cm. Perimeter?
questions.model: Teacher: same as a 9 by 5 rectangle: 2 × (9 + 5) = 28 cm.

questions.q: Total length 12 cm; one part 7 cm. Missing part?
How many sides does an L-shape have?
A 5 by 2 rectangle of squares. Area?
questions.model: Teacher counts 5 in each row, 2 rows: 10 squares.

questions.q: 8 whole and 2 half squares?
Is area measured in cm or cm²?
12 cm by 5 cm. Area?
Area 54 m², length 9 m. Width?
A square of side 8 cm. Area?
12 whole and 5 half-or-more squares?
Do we count a square that is a quarter covered?
Why do two pupils get slightly different estimates?
questions.a: They judge the part squares differently

questions.q: 10 cm by 3 cm. Perimeter?
Big question: why only two measurements?
questions.a: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so we double length + width

questions.q: L-shape outer sides 7 m and 4 m. Perimeter?
Big question: how do we find a missing side?
questions.a: Use opposite sides: the parts on one side add up to the whole on the other

questions.q: Area of a 3 by 3 square?
Big question: what does area measure?
questions.a: The space inside a shape, in square units

questions.q: 6 m by 5 m area?
Big question: why does length × width give the area?
questions.a: The squares form rows: width rows of length squares, like an array

questions.q: 8 whole + 4 half or more?
Big question: how can we find the area of a leaf?
questions.a: Count whole squares and squares half or more covered, then add: an estimate
